subject: ent
title: Sinusitis and its complications

steps.tx: **Acute rhinosinusitis** is usually viral (under ten days, improving), while acute bacterial disease declares by three patterns: persistent symptoms over ten days without improvement, severe onset (fever over 39, purulence and facial pain for three to four days), or double worsening after initial recovery. Maxillary sinus dominates adults; ethmoids dominate children because frontal and sphenoid sinuses pneumatise later (frontal from about age seven onward). Ostiomeatal obstruction, viral ciliary failure and allergy underpin most episodes.
steps.say: Cold over ten days, severe from start, or better then worse: bacterial sinusitis. Frontal sinuses arrive late in childhood.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Chronic disease and imaging discipline: CT is for complications, recurrence, surgery planning or immunocompromise, not routine colds. Examination and endoscopy show middle meatal pus, polyps or oedema. Antibiotics (local first line, e.g. amoxicillin patterns) reserve for bacterial criteria with analgesia, saline irrigation and intranasal steroids as symptomatic backbone. Dental roots (upper premolars and molars) infect maxillary sinus unilaterally, needing dental source control.
steps.say: Scan sinuses for complications or surgery, not every cold. One sided maxillary disease smells dental.

steps.tx: **Orbital complications** of ethmoid sinusitis (Chandler groups) escalate from preseptal cellulitis through orbital cellulitis, subperiosteal abscess, orbital abscess to cavernous sinus thrombosis. Proptosis, painful restricted eye movements, chemosis, vision change or bilateral signs are emergencies needing contrast CT, IV antibiotics and ENT ophthalmology drainage decisions. Children through thin lamina papyracea are classic victims.
steps.say: Swollen eye plus painful movements plus sinusitis is orbital emergency until scanned. Bilateral eye signs mean cavernous sinus.

steps.tx: Intracranial and bone complications include frontal osteomyelitis with forehead swelling (**Pott puffy tumour**), epidural and subdural empyema, meningitis, frontal lobe abscess and cavernous sinus thrombosis (bilateral ophthalmoplegia, chemosis, trigeminal signs, sepsis). Sphenoid disease threatens cavernous sinus, pituitary and carotid neighbours. Functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) restores ostiomeatal ventilation in chronic or complicated disease refractory to medical therapy, respecting orbit and skull base landmarks.
steps.say: Puffy forehead over sinusitis is bone infection. FESS opens drainage; orbit and brain sit millimetres away.
